acquisition_method.evidence: experiment types: Bottom-up proteomics; Data-dependent acquisition
The mass spectrometer was operated in positive, data-dependent acquisition mode, commencing with a full MS scan across an m/z range of 300–2000 at a resolution of 75000.

alkylation_concentration.evidence: Subsequently, proteins were alkylated with 15 mM iodoacetamide in the dark for 30 min at room temperature.

alkylation_reagent.evidence: Subsequently, proteins were alkylated with 15 mM iodoacetamide in the dark for 30 min at room temperature.

cleavage_agent.evidence: Digestion was carried out overnight by adding two aliquots of trypsin (first at a 1:40 w/w ratio of trypsin and second at a 1:50 w/w ratio, with a 4-hour interval between additions) at 37 °C with agitation (800 rpm).

collision_energy.evidence: Fragmentation was conducted with a normalized collision energy of 30, and MS/MS scans were acquired at a resolution of 30000.

fragmentation_method.evidence: MS/MS acquisition was performed via higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) for the ten most intense precursor ions, with quadrupole isolation set to a 1.4 m/z width.

instrument.evidence: LC-MS/MS analysis was performed for each sample using a nanoLC EASY 1200 system (LC-030378, Thermo Scientific, USA) coupled to a Q Exactive Plus mass spectrometer (03893L, Thermo Scientific, USA) at the Mass Spectrometry Unit of CENTD (Instituto Butantan, Brazil).

labeling.evidence: Protein abundances were quantified using the MaxQuant label-free quantification (LFQ) algorithm, which normalizes chromatographic peak integrations.
